rv.q: Birch has crafted a rich, haunting, technically dazzling script, in which the women cast eerie shadows through time.
The play is both riveting and static.
And yet, finally, such vague misgivings pale beside the essential bravery and daring of it all.
Though it is hard to imagine anyone actually enjoying this show, it will be admired for its assured production.
"Anatomy of a Suicide" is a shimmeringly powerful puzzle play that respects, and rewards, the attention of its audience.
When their house is finally revealed at the end we, the audience feel the light flood in and the weight from Bonnie lifted as she is able to finally put her past to rest.
Sadly, Birch and Mitchell are better at representing darkness than at throwing light on their subject.
It does, in a way, deserve a prize — for the most obtuse script of the year.

cn.t: An audacious, structurally ambitious exploration of suicide across three generations earns widespread praise for Birch's writing and Mitchell's direction, though one critic finds the experimental format conceals thin storytelling.
